# leaflet-tual v3

> Opinionated whiteboard-style annotation toolset (pen, arrows, shapes, notes, text, rulers, area, laser pointer, pages) for Leaflet maps. Everything stored in geographic coordinates.

Draw on a map the way you draw on a design canvas. Coordinates are always `GeoPoint` (`{ lat, lng }`), keeping annotations attached to the ground while the map pans and zooms.

## Navigation & Quick Links
- Website: https://leaflet-tual.dev
- Interactive Demo: https://leaflet-tual.dev/demo
- GitHub Repository: https://github.com/yusufarsln98/leaflet-tual
- npm Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/leaflet-tual
- SKILL.md Specification: https://leaflet-tual.dev/SKILL.md

## Core Invariants & Rules
1. **Store geography, never pixels.** Every persisted coordinate is a `GeoPoint` (`{ lat, lng }`). Never put screen `{ x, y }` in an item.
2. **Do geometry in world space.** Aspect locks, 45° snapping, circle radii, curve offsets, hit tests and resizing run in a zoom-independent plane (`toWorld` / `fromWorld`), never in current-zoom pixels. Squares stay square and curves keep their shape at every zoom level and latitude.
3. **Use hex colors and explicit sizes.** Colors are hex strings like `#2F6FEB`; transparency is a separate `opacity` value. Widths are `'s' | 'm' | 'l'`, text sizes are `'s' | 'm' | 'l' | 'xl'`.
4. **Change the look through tokens**, not by overriding library internals with CSS selectors.
5. **Every UI word is a translation token.** Provide custom `translations` or set default tokens.
6. **Change the toolbar through the `toolbar` prop.**
7. **One document, one change callback.** State is a plain JSON `Doc`. Save from `onChange` only when `info.committed` is `true`.
8. **Controlled or uncontrolled, never both.** Pass `value` or `defaultValue`. Undo and redo work in both modes and report through `onChange`.
9. **Mutate through the controller** (`add`, `update`, `remove`). Never edit `doc` or `items` in place.
10. **Modifiers are built in.** `Shift` locks aspect (1:1) and snaps angles to 45°. `Alt` resizes from the center.
11. **Validate untrusted JSON** with `parseDoc(input)` before `load`.
12. **Map context.** Inside `<MapContainer>`, `<LeafletTual>` finds the map itself. Outside it, pass `map={mapInstance}`.

## Data Model

```ts
export type GeoPoint = { lat: number; lng: number }

export interface Doc {
  activePageId: string  // id of the active page
  pages: Page[]
}

export interface Page {
  id: string
  name: string
  view?: { center: GeoPoint; zoom: number }
  items: Record<string, Item>
  order: string[]
}

export interface Style {
  color?: string
  fillColor?: string
  strokeColor?: string
  textColor?: string
  opacity?: number
  width?: 's' | 'm' | 'l' | number
  dash?: 'solid' | 'dashed' | 'dotted' | 'none'
  size?: 's' | 'm' | 'l' | 'xl'
  weight?: 'regular' | 'bold'
  fontStyle?: 'normal' | 'italic'
  textDecoration?: 'none' | 'underline'
  underline?: boolean
  list?: 'none' | 'bullet'
  bullets?: boolean
  align?: 'left' | 'center' | 'right'
}

export type ArrowKind = 'linear' | 'curved' | 'elbow'
export type Head = 'triangle' | 'open' | 'none'
export type ShapeKind =
  | 'square' | 'circle' | 'star' | 'actor'
  | 'triangle' | 'diamond' | 'hexagon' | 'marker'
export type LabelPosition = 'top' | 'center' | 'bottom'

export interface ArrowItem {
  id: string
  type: 'arrow'
  kind: ArrowKind
  from: GeoPoint
  to: GeoPoint
  via?: GeoPoint
  heads?: { start?: Head; end?: Head }
  label?: string
  style?: Style
  createdAt: number
}

export interface ShapeItem {
  id: string
  type: 'shape'
  kind: ShapeKind
  at: GeoPoint
  width: number
  height: number
  label?: string
  labelPosition?: LabelPosition   // default 'center'
  style?: Style
  createdAt: number
}

export interface FreedrawItem {
  id: string
  type: 'freedraw'
  points: GeoPoint[]
  style?: Style
  createdAt: number
}

export interface PenPoint {
  at: GeoPoint
  in?: GeoPoint     // incoming bezier control point (absolute geography)
  out?: GeoPoint    // outgoing bezier control point (absolute geography)
}

export interface PenItem {
  id: string
  type: 'pen'
  points: PenPoint[]
  closed?: boolean
  style?: Style
  createdAt: number
}

export interface RulerItem {
  id: string
  type: 'ruler'
  from: GeoPoint
  to: GeoPoint
  unit?: 'metric' | 'imperial'
  label?: string
  style?: Style
  createdAt: number
}

export interface AreaItem {
  id: string
  type: 'area'
  points: GeoPoint[]
  unit?: 'metric' | 'imperial'
  label?: string
  style?: Style
  createdAt: number
}

export interface NoteItem {
  id: string
  type: 'note'
  at: GeoPoint
  width?: number
  height?: number
  title?: string
  text: string
  style?: Style
  createdAt: number
}

export interface TextItem {
  id: string
  type: 'text'
  at: GeoPoint
  text: string
  style?: Style
  createdAt: number
}

export type Item =
  | ArrowItem | ShapeItem | FreedrawItem | PenItem | RulerItem | AreaItem
  | NoteItem | TextItem
```

Pen paths remain editable after drawing: with the Select tool, drag an anchor or a bezier control handle to reshape the path. Dragging one control handle mirrors the opposite handle around its anchor. Area polygons support dragging handles to reshape polygon boundaries. Middle-click drag pans the map even when items are selected.

## Quick Start (React)

```tsx
import { MapContainer, TileLayer } from 'react-leaflet'
import { LeafletTual } from 'leaflet-tual/react'
import 'leaflet/dist/leaflet.css'
import 'leaflet-tual/styles.css'

export function MapView() {
  return (
    <MapContainer center={[41.01, 28.97]} zoom={13} style={{ height: '100vh' }}>
      <TileLayer url="https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png" />
      <LeafletTual onChange={(doc, { committed }) => committed && save(doc)} />
    </MapContainer>
  )
}
```

`<LeafletTual>` props are all optional. Item properties are edited from the contextual toolbar, the optional sidebar inspector, or the right-click menu.

## Toolbar, Sidebar & Theming

The toolbar is a stack of Leaflet-style control islands: **Page → Tools → More**. Each island has a thin border, a small radius and one square control per action. The page island shows the active page name; open it to switch, rename, add or delete pages. Page renaming lives in the page settings menu rather than inline in the toolbar. In vertical toolbars the page control collapses to its icon so the island stays square. Undo, redo, fit-in-view and the sidebar toggle live in the More menu at the end. The position controls the layout: top/bottom edges lay out horizontally, left/right edges lay out vertically; every edge supports start, center and end alignment. When the sidebar is open, the built-in toolbar is pinned to the top center regardless of the configured position. Tools with variants expose a small corner triangle; the main icon activates the tool with its last-used variant.

```tsx
<LeafletTual
  toolbar={{
    position: 'top-left',      // default; horizontal along the top edge
    tools: ['select', 'freedraw', 'pen', 'arrow', 'shape', 'ruler', 'area', 'laser', 'note'],
    pages: true,
    history: true,
  }}
  themeTokens={{
    surface: 'var(--app-panel)',
    surfaceActive: 'var(--app-accent)',
    text: 'var(--app-text)',
    textActive: 'var(--app-accent-contrast)',
    accent: 'var(--app-accent)',
    border: 'var(--app-border)',
    divider: 'var(--app-border-muted)',
    radius: '6px',
    controlSize: '30px',
  }}
/>
```

`ToolbarOptions`: `position` (default `'top-left'`; top/bottom are horizontal, left/right vertical, with start/center/end alignment on every edge), `orientation` (only used by `'inline'` toolbars), `tools`, `pages` (default `true`), `history` (default `true`, renders undo/redo/fit in the More menu). Pass `toolbar={false}` to hide the built-in toolbar. External `<Toolbar>` accepts `sidebarOpen` and `onToggleSidebar` so its More menu can control an external sidebar.

Keyboard shortcuts are enabled by default. Pass `shortcuts={false}` to `<LeafletTual>` to disable them; a standalone `<Toolbar shortcuts={false}>` also hides its shortcut hints.

Set `sidebar` to open the right-side properties and layers inspector initially: `<LeafletTual sidebar />`. The toolbar's More menu toggles it, the inspector header has a close button, and `onSidebarChange` keeps external state in sync. It shows the page/layer tree and style controls for the current selection; selecting a tree item focuses it on the map, and right-clicking a tree item opens the shared context menu. The More button at the end of the selected item's contextual toolbar also opens the inspector. While the sidebar is visible, the contextual item toolbar is hidden so properties are edited in one place, and the built-in toolbar is pinned to the top center. The standalone `<Sidebar controller={tual} map={map} onClose={...} />` component is also exported; `onClose` is only needed when the host can hide it. The built-in sidebar stays hidden in read-only mode.

`ThemeTokens` themes only the chrome (toolbar, sidebar, menus, popovers and contextual tooltip), never annotation items. Available tokens: `surface`, `surfaceActive`, `surfaceMuted`, `text`, `textMuted`, `textActive`, `accent`, `border`, `divider`, `focus`, `radius`, `radiusSm`, `radiusLg`, `shadow`, `shadowPopup`, `controlSize`, `groupGap`, `iconSize`, `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, and `variables` for extra CSS custom properties. Values may be colors or CSS variable references. `themeTokens` is also accepted by `createLeafletTual(map, { themeTokens })` and external `<Toolbar themeTokens={...} />`.

Reusable chrome controls are exported from `leaflet-tual/react` for custom panels: `Button`, `IconButton`, `PillButton`, `SegmentedControl`, `Popover`, `DropdownMenu`, `DropdownItem`, `ConfirmPopover`, `Select`, `NumberField`, `TextField`, `PropertyRow`, `Collapsible`, `ColorSwatch`, `ColorSwatchList`, `ColorSwatchControls`, `CustomColorPicker`, `ColorDropdown`, `TypographyDropdown`, `TextFormattingControls`, `LabelPositionDropdown`, `BorderPopover`, `useOutsideDismiss`, `useWheelGuard`, `useLeafletDomGuard`, `useLeafletDisableClick`, `disableMapInteractions`, `createLeafletControl`, and `createControlContainer`. Wrap a custom panel with `useLeafletDomGuard()` or give it the `tual-panel` class to isolate it from map gestures.

## Vanilla JS Core (No React)

```ts
import L from 'leaflet'
import { createLeafletTual, emptyDoc } from 'leaflet-tual'
import 'leaflet-tual/styles.css'

const map = L.map('map').setView([41.01, 28.97], 13)
const tual = createLeafletTual(map, {
  defaultValue: emptyDoc(),
  onChange: (doc, info) => info.committed && save(doc),
})

tual.setTool('freedraw') // or tual.setTool('pen') for the bezier pen
tual.on('select', (items) => console.log(items))
// cleanup
tual.destroy()
```

The vanilla core mounts the canvas only. Render `<Toolbar>` from `leaflet-tual/react` or build your own controls with `setTool` / `setStyle`.

## Controller API (`useLeafletTual` & `createLeafletTual`)

State:
- `doc: Doc`
- `items: Item[]`
- `tool: ToolId`
- `variant: ToolVariant | null`
- `style: Style`
- `selection: string[]`
- `selected: Item[]`
- `readOnly: boolean`
- `canUndo: boolean`
- `canRedo: boolean`
- `translations: TranslationTokens`

Actions:
- `setTool(tool, variant?)`
- `setStyle(patch)` (selection-aware)
- `setTranslations(patch)`
- `add(item)`
- `update(id, patch, committed?)`
- `updateMany(patches, committed?)`
- `duplicate(ids?)`
- `reorder(ids, action)`
- `bringToFront(ids?)` / `sendToBack(ids?)` / `bringForward(ids?)` / `sendBackward(ids?)`
- `remove(ids?)`
- `clear()`
- `select(ids)` / `selectAll()`
- `edit(id)`
- `undo()` / `redo()`
- `fit(target)` ('all', 'selection', or item id)
- `load(doc)`
- `setReadOnly(boolean)`
- `pages.list`, `pages.active`, `pages.add(name?)`, `pages.rename(id, name)`, `pages.remove(id)`, `pages.move(id, toIndex)`, `pages.select(id)`

## Geometry Utilities
- `toWorld(geo)` / `fromWorld(point)`: Spherical Mercator world meters projection
- `geoToScreen(map, geo)` / `screenToGeo(map, point)`
- `lockAspect(anchor, target, ratio = 1)` (world space)
- `snapAngle(anchor, target, step = 45)` (world space)
- `defaultVia(from, to, curvature = 0.25)` (world space)
- `distance(a, b)` / `pathDistance(points)` / `formatDistance(meters, unit, tokens?)`
- `polygonArea(points)` / `polygonCentroid(points)` / `formatArea(sqMeters, unit, tokens?)`
- `bounds(item)` / `hitTest(item, point, tolerance)`
- `resolveColor(hex)`
